Method and AI prediction (written before measurements)

Method. A two interval forced choice task compares masker alone with masker plus probe. The listener identifies the interval containing the probe. A two-down, one-up staircase adjusts the probe level, beginning with 6 dB steps and reducing to 2 dB after two reversals. A track ends after 8 reversals; its threshold is the mean of the last 6 reversal levels. Quiet baselines use probe versus silence. Masking amount is the masked threshold minus the baseline threshold at the same probe frequency.

Prediction before data collection. I predict that probe thresholds will be highest near the masker frequency and will fall as probe frequency moves away. I expect the masking pattern to be broader on the high-frequency side than the low-frequency side, with curve width changing across masker frequencies because auditory filters and critical-band widths vary with frequency. The measured curves may depart from this prediction because the experiment uses pure tones, uncalibrated playback, one listener, and a finite number of trials.

AI suggestion to evaluate after data collection. Compare the prediction above with the actual curves. Record one concrete suggestion that you changed or rejected and the measurement or course concept that led you to do so. Do not fill this in until you have results.

Use headphones in a quiet setting if available. Keep playback comfortable and take breaks. dBFS values describe the digital signal; they cannot be converted to sound pressure level without calibration.

QUICK TUTORIAL · ABOUT 2 MINUTES

Learn the listening task

First set the device volume low and comfortable. Use Play sound check on the setup panel. It uses your selected masker frequency and level with an intentionally obvious probe one octave higher; it does not change or add anything to your experiment data.

How to set up the measurement
  1. Keep the masker frequency and level fixed during a track.
  2. Each track tests one probe frequency. The full set steps through frequencies around 500, 1000, and 2000 Hz.
  3. Quiet baseline tracks play the probe against silence; masked tracks compare masker alone with masker plus probe.

In each pair, both intervals contain the masker. One has an extra probe tone. The order is random, so listen for the interval that sounds different: a second pitch, a small change in tone quality, or beating when the tones are close.

Practice staircase

Listen to both intervals, then choose where the extra probe was. The probe starts clearly audible, then gets quieter. Two correct answers in a row lower it; a wrong answer raises it.
